tasks.short: Collect employee information through prescribed questions and confirm the answers.

steps.what: Check the prescribed questionnaire and instructions for this interview.
Look up existing employee details before asking for missing information.
Ask the employee the standard factual questions.
Clarify misunderstood questions and help the employee explain unusual circumstances.
Record the answers and read them back for employee confirmation.

loop.input: Structured answers and interviewer clarification notes.
loop.output: Draft answers mapped to questionnaire fields, with supporting note references.
loop.check: Validate field types; show every inferred mapping; require employee confirmation before submission.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt; unresolved fields return to the interviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured answers need no model, but free-text clarification notes need interpretation.

steps.what: Enter confirmed answers into the employee record.

tasks.design: Configure a questionnaire in the {HCM} or {WORKFLOW}, prefilled from authorised employee records, and remove questions without a justified collection purpose. Employees complete routine fields directly; interviewers handle clarification, while a bounded extraction loop prepares notes for employee confirmation and validated entry into the {HCM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interview scripts, notes and employee records sit apart. Unusual answers and accessibility needs make a single rigid form insufficient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form controls and record interfaces cover routine collection. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings and validation; bounded extraction can handle clarification notes.
tasks.still_hard: Accessible assisted completion, multilingual ambiguity and lawful collection of sensitive fields need careful design. Religion is special-category data under GDPR and is not a default HR intake field.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice confusion and help employees describe circumstances without steering their answers.

ambition.what: Accessible assisted intake for employees who cannot complete the standard digital form

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends more time on assisted intake and ambiguous answers. They gain discretion to choose the assistance channel, while substantive HR decisions remain with authorised roles.

reach.learn: Field ownership, effective dates and the difference between recording facts and approving changes.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee self-service changes flowing to payroll; this supports the records pattern, not this complete intake design.
Forms, prefilling and validation can replace routine interviewer collection; the time shares and build estimates are planning assumptions.
GDPR requires a justified purpose and an appropriate legal basis, including additional conditions for special-category data.

assumptions: The HR interpretation is factual employee intake, not candidate assessment.
Time shares describe an illustrative interview with clarification, not measured company data.
The interviewer remains available for assisted completion; employee effort does not disappear.
Automatic writes cover confirmed factual fields, not pay, benefit or employment decisions.
Build ranges assume one questionnaire and one employee-record interface. Consultation and access ranges cover working effort; external waiting may be longer.
Conversation-heavy priors fit clarification, but routine factual collection is sufficiently structured for configured forms.
unknowns: Which questions are actually asked and why each field is required.
Available self-service features, record interfaces and write permissions.
The proportion of employees needing assisted completion.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which accessibility and language options reduce assisted-completion failures?
Can existing field controls support the questionnaire without custom code?
new_work: Maintain questionnaire versions and collection purposes.
Handle failed submissions and duplicate records.

tasks.short: Find invalid or missing interview data, investigate the cause and report unresolved problems.

steps.what: Check completed intake records against required fields and validation instructions.
Compare exceptions with interview notes to understand missing or inconsistent answers.

loop.input: Validity exceptions and relevant clarification notes.
loop.output: Suggested problem category with quoted supporting passages and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Require source passages and an allowed category; interviewer confirms interpretation.
loop.stop: One classification pass; unsupported or ambiguous cases remain unclassified for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect missing fields, but narrative contradictions and misunderstood questions require reading.

steps.what: Contact the employee to clarify the problem and request corrections.
Write an unresolved-data report and send it to the responsible HR specialist.

loop.input: Reviewed exception assessment, correction notes and report template.
loop.output: Draft report separating observed facts, attempted corrections and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Every factual claim links to a record or note; interviewer reviews before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; incomplete evidence produces a template for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative causes vary; fixed fields alone do not explain why collection failed.

steps.what: Decide whether to accept, correct or escalate the disputed data.
Record the resolution and update the exception status.

tasks.design: Run explicit validation rules on intake records in the {HCM} and manage exceptions in the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded loops classify narrative problems and draft evidence-linked reports; interviewers clarify answers and HR specialists approve disputed resolutions before the {HCM} is updated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Validation instructions were separate from collection screens. Explanations and resolutions were scattered across notes and the {EMAIL}.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable checks handle objective defects. Small reading and drafting loops can prepare the narrative work without deciding whether an employee is credible.
tasks.still_hard: An unusual answer may be valid. Resolving conflicting accounts, changing a poorly designed question and deciding whether collection is appropriate still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a confusing question from an unreliable answer and investigate without treating employees as suspects.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on recurring questionnaire defects

tasks.altitude: The interviewer handles fewer mechanical checks and brings documented patterns to a weekly intake review. They can propose question changes; the HR process owner approves them.

reach.learn: Root-cause analysis, evidence standards and correction versus escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Deterministic checks can detect missing fields and incompatible values; narrative review and estimated savings remain design assumptions.
The documented Amsterdam welfare case shows that automated flags did not establish better judgement than caseworkers; it is a caution, not an HR result.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: This task checks information quality rather than fraud, employee performance or hiring suitability.
Objective validation is separated from accepting disputed facts.
Shares include the HR specialist handoff and are illustrative.
The low-rule-coverage prior fits interpreting exceptions, while completeness checks have higher rule coverage.
Build ranges cover an initial rule set and one intake workflow; access and consultation waiting may exceed the stated working effort.
unknowns: Existing validation rules and exception volumes.
Who may accept disputed data or authorise corrections.
Whether notes are sufficiently complete to support classification.
National rules governing consultation if exception data could monitor staff.
research_questions: Which validation rules produce false alarms on legitimate employee circumstances?
Can recurring defects be reported in aggregate without exposing individual interview notes?
new_work: Review narrative classifications and draft reports.
Investigate false alarms and missed defects.
Maintain validation rules when questionnaires change.
Monitor unresolved cases and their assigned owners.

tasks.short: Verify coverage for employee services and arrange payment where coverage is incomplete.

steps.what: Collect the service request, provider details and authority to request coverage information.
Check the provider portal for current coverage and authorisation requirements.
Read coverage conditions, exclusions and any unresolved provider qualifications.

loop.input: Provider response, applicable coverage wording and requested service.
loop.output: Coverage conditions, limits, expiry dates and unresolved questions with source passages.
loop.check: Validate amounts and dates against the source; benefits specialist confirms the summary.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; ambiguous coverage returns to the provider through a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Provider qualifications may be narrative. Structured responses bypass the model entirely.

steps.what: Calculate the uncovered amount using service prices and confirmed coverage.
Discuss the uncovered amount and permitted payment options with the employee.
Approve the arrangement and issue the confirmed payment terms.

tasks.design: An access-controlled case in the {WORKFLOW} requests minimum coverage data through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and stores the response in the {DOCS}. A bounded loop extracts narrative terms, deterministic calculations in the {ERP} show the uncovered amount, and approved payment terms are issued only after employee acceptance and finance approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coverage terms differ between providers, access is fragmented and negotiated arrangements need accountable approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Where provider interfaces exist, ordinary integrations can retrieve coverage. Bounded extraction can prepare a checked summary of narrative terms, while calculations remain plain code.
tasks.still_hard: A coverage check is not a payment guarantee. Provider access, disputed coverage, sensitive information and regulated financing arrangements may dominate cost.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty clearly and discuss affordability without pressuring the employee into an unsuitable arrangement.

ambition.what: A pre-service estimate of uncovered employee costs

tasks.altitude: The interviewer spends less time navigating provider records and calculating amounts. They can present approved options earlier; they gain no authority to grant coverage, credit or payroll deductions.

reach.task: Resolve unclear benefit coverage with providers.
reach.learn: Coverage terminology, provider evidence requirements and boundaries between estimates and binding commitments.

evidence.claim: Provider integration, checked extraction and deterministic cost calculations are a proposed architecture; the digest contains no direct benefits-verification case.
GDPR imposes additional conditions on processing health data; an employee's operational authorisation alone does not establish every required legal basis.
Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects are constrained by GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: This is a conditional benefits-service intake scenario. Insurance verification and service financing are not typical duties in every HR department.
The employer has a legitimate role in coordinating payment; clinical records and diagnoses remain outside interviewer access.
A supported provider interface exists. Without one, portal checking remains manual and the integration estimate must be revised.
Payment options come from an approved policy. Credit underwriting and payroll deductions require separate assessment and authority.
Employee acceptance is recorded before finance issues binding terms.
Time shares describe this specialised scenario. The API-heavy prior is not proof that a particular provider offers access.
Build ranges cover one provider. Consultation, contracting and access waiting can be substantially longer than working effort.
unknowns: Whether this task exists in the customer's HR remit.
Which providers permit coverage queries and through which interfaces.
Who is liable for uncovered charges and whether financing involves regulated credit.
Applicable GDPR bases, special-category conditions and national rules.
Who can approve arrangements and how employee acceptance is recorded.
research_questions: What does each provider response establish, and how long is it valid?
Which proposed payment options require specialist credit or employment-law review?
new_work: Handle unavailable providers and stale coverage responses.
Maintain provider mappings, prices and payment policies.
Reconcile estimates against final charges and provider payments.

tasks.short: Handle HR office enquiries, maintain staff records and coordinate applicable service billing and receipts.

steps.what: Read incoming enquiries and identify the responsible team.

loop.input: Enquiry text and an approved routing taxonomy.
loop.output: Queue assignment and a minimal case description.
loop.check: Use explicit routing rules first; validate allowed queues and access restrictions.
loop.stop: One classification pass; ambiguous or sensitive cases enter a restricted manual triage queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text enquiries may lack explicit routing terms. Structured submissions use rules only.

steps.what: Find the applicable HR guidance and answer the enquiry.

loop.input: Enquiry and current, authorised HR guidance passages.
loop.output: Draft response with supporting guidance references.
loop.check: Check source version and employee access; HR assistant approves before sending.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one draft; missing or conflicting guidance triggers specialist referral.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied wording and context need a short tailored explanation; fixed requests use templates.

steps.what: Enter authorised staff changes into the employee record.
Forward approved service charges and payment terms to finance.
Prepare and issue the invoice against the authorised billing instruction.
Match incoming payments to invoices and record outstanding balances.

tasks.design: Use the {HELPDESK} for enquiry routing and reviewed answers grounded in current {DOCS}, while configured approvals feed authorised changes into the {HCM}. Where service billing belongs to this desk, the {WORKFLOW} passes approved charges to the {ERP}, which generates reviewed invoices and matches exact payment references from the {BANK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: A shared mailbox connects enquiries, employee changes and finance handoffs. Each team re-enters information because authorisation and record identifiers do not travel with the request.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured case routing, employee self-service and invoice matching already cover much of the work. Bounded loops are useful only for unstructured routing and response drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive enquiries need restricted queues. Record-change authority, disputed charges and unmatched receipts still require clear ownership and human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a routine enquiry masks a grievance, hardship or confidential issue and arrange the right human response.

ambition.what: A single status view for employee requests and related service charges

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time forwarding messages and copying approved changes. They can coordinate stalled cases across HR and finance, without gaining authority to approve benefits or waive debts.

reach.task: Check employee-change effective dates before the payroll cutoff.
reach.learn: Payroll cutoffs, correction procedures and which changes require separate payroll approval.

reach.task: Separate routine policy enquiries from cases needing confidential handling.
reach.learn: Escalation criteria, restricted access and neutral case summaries.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee self-service changes flowing to payroll and HR questions grounded in collective-agreement material.
TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base or opens a prefilled request, supporting the answer-and-handover pattern.
Approved invoice generation and exact-reference payment matching can use configured finance controls; these estimates are not documented case results.

assumptions: This broad occupational task is interpreted primarily as HR enquiries and staff-record administration.
Telemarketing and patient billing are sector-specific variants, not assumed general HR duties.
The billing steps apply only to the specialised employee-service scenario described in the coverage task.
Time shares illustrate a desk with that billing remit and include finance handoffs. A general HR desk needs a different allocation.
Approved staff changes already contain the required authorisation; automation does not approve substantive employment changes.
Payment matching accepts exact, unambiguous matches; partial, duplicate and disputed payments become exceptions.
The mailbox share is higher than the supplied prior because this scenario uses a shared mailbox for cross-team handoffs.
Build ranges assume existing systems and supported interfaces. National consultation and access waiting may exceed working effort.
unknowns: Which office duties actually belong to this role.
Whether the desk handles any billable employee services.
Existing enquiry queues, guidance ownership and response volumes.
Supported interfaces and approval controls across HR and finance.
National rules and consultation requirements if new reporting could monitor employees.
research_questions: Can current enquiry and self-service configuration remove the mailbox handoffs?
Which payment exceptions need manual investigation rather than automatic allocation?
new_work: Review answer drafts and maintain current guidance.
Handle restricted, ambiguous and misrouted enquiries.
Review invoices and reconcile unmatched payments.
Maintain routing rules, permissions and integration alerts.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward assisted information collection, clarification and documented exception handling. Routine entry and handoffs shrink; hiring, benefit entitlement, credit and employment decisions remain with their authorised decision makers.
reach: Help HR assistants prepare complete employee-change cases.
Support benefits specialists with checked coverage evidence where this service exists.
Give HR specialists recurring evidence of confusing questions and collection failures.
skills_to_grow: Data minimisation and handling sensitive employee information.
Checking extracted facts against their sources.
Designing field validation and testing exceptions.
Understanding approval boundaries and effective dates.
Investigating failed handoffs across HR and finance.
role.ambitious_version: Run an accessible intake service that helps employees complete difficult requests, provides clear status updates and brings recurring collection defects to HR for correction.
